These two act on Home after the songs have arrived, whatever Quick picks is set to. Neither chooses which songs are fetched. Tidy Home rows reaches every recommendation row on the screen. Ranking touches only Quick picks, and stands aside when the engine built that row, under Best recommendations or Try both, since it is already in the order the engine built.\n\nThe group below is the engine\'s, and Try both runs the engine too, so those settings act there as well. Exclusions are the exception: bans and snoozes filter every row whatever the source, through the pass above, and rests can be sent everywhere too.

One pass runs down Home, Quick picks, Forgotten favourites, Keep listening, Similar to, then the feed, and no row shows a song an earlier row has. Two cards count as one when their titles agree after brackets and a spaced dash suffix go, so live, remastered and video fold into the original, but only if the first artist matches.\n\nQuick picks also drops this session\'s songs and anything you heard 30 seconds and 45 percent of in the last day. Nothing fills a gap, so a row can come up short. On by default. Off, and bans and snoozes stop filtering these rows, though Best recommendations still refuses them itself.

It reorders a row built elsewhere. Each song scores on the same twelve measures the engine uses: how recently and often you played it, whether you liked it, how strong that artist is with you, whether it is new, and how often you have scrolled past it in the last fortnight. Nothing is added and nothing is removed.\n\nThe order is drawn in proportion to those scores rather than sorted, so a refresh reorders. It runs on the Your library row, and within each tier of the YouTube row, the shelf first. It stands aside when the engine built the row, under Best recommendations or Try both. On by default.

The row is twenty cards from five lanes: related, songs YouTube lists beside up to sixteen seeds from your listening (seven by default); again, songs you played through in the last fortnight (four); artist, songs by artists you play most, left alone a fortnight (four); rediscover, songs quiet for forty five days you kept returning to (three); explore, songs you have never played through (two).\n\nAdventurousness, Familiarity and New songs only apply while Quick picks source, under Library and content, is Best recommendations or Try both. Exclusions below always filter this row, the other sources only while Tidy home rows is on. It is marked experimental and still learning.

Explore gets five percent of the row plus up to thirty more in proportion to the slider, off the top; related, again, artist and rediscover then split what is left, so all four give ground as you raise it. At the default of 15 that is two of twenty; 0 still gives one and 100 gives seven.\n\nThe lane prefers artists you have never played, but when it cannot find twice its quota of those it fills up with new songs by artists you already know. A change waits for the next build: three hours, a new session, a new day part, or a pull to refresh.

Again takes this share of what is left after explore; related, artist and rediscover shrink to pay. The default 25 gives four of twenty, 0 gives none and 60 as many as eleven. The lane holds songs you got about halfway through in the last fortnight, minus this session and anything heard well in the last hour.\n\nWear counts plays over ninety days, each discounted by age: one today counts whole, a week back a third. Ten of those and a song starts losing score, thirty and it loses most. Going well past your usual gap pushes it down, not up, so the lane favours songs still in rotation.

New here means never heard past roughly the halfway mark, not never started: a song you have begun and skipped early still counts. While it is on, again, artist and rediscover are switched off, the whole twenty goes to explore, and related is drawn on only for the overflow, itself cut to songs you have not heard. Adventurousness and Familiarity stop mattering, though their card counts above still say otherwise.\n\nCandidates are what YouTube lists beside songs you have played, plus library songs you have never played, so the row can come up short. Under eight cards Quick picks hands over to the library row, then the YouTube shelf.

The line names the strongest thing behind the card: the largest positive term of its score, one of twelve worked out for every candidate. That is why the wording changes, from because you played something, to you finish a lot of this artist, to one you liked. Two say something else: a song new to you says so, and a card drawn from its lane by chance, not by score, is a wildcard.\n\nThe reasons are worked out when the row is built whether you show them or not, so the line costs nothing. It sits where the song\'s length would be, on the engine\'s cards only. On by default.

Long-press a card in Quick picks for three choices. Not this song and Never this artist hold until you lift them. Less of this artist is not a dial: it takes that artist out for a month, then lapses. Banning a song covers its other versions, so the live take and the remix go too, while artist entries match the card\'s main artist, so a guest appearance can still get through.\n\nAll of this touches the recommendation rows only: search, your library, playlists and radio are never filtered. This page lists what is in force with its expiry; Lift removes one, with an Undo if you slip.

A rest is written when you press next before the halfway point of a song you have liked or already played three times, and only after thirty seconds have actually played, so a quick skip past something costs nothing. The song then stays out of the Best recommendations row for a week and appears on the Exclusions page with its date, where you can lift it early.\n\nOff by default, and nothing is rested while listen history is paused. Rests always reach the engine\'s own row. They reach the other Home rows as well whenever Best recommendations is your Quick picks source, or when the switch below is on.

With this on, a rested song is also kept out of the YouTube Music shelf, your library\'s Quick picks, Forgotten favourites, Keep listening, Similar to, and YouTube\'s home feed. Those lists are not built here, so the song is dropped after the row arrives: the row comes back shorter unless the pool has something spare to fill the gap, and a section left with nothing is not shown.\n\nIt covers rests only; bans and snoozes already filter every row. It needs Tidy home rows on, since the filter runs in that pass, and it changes nothing while Quick picks is already Best recommendations, where rests reach every row anyway.

Everything below is the engine marking its own homework in the open, where you can watch it fail. The numbers are worked out on this phone from your own listening, and none of it leaves unless you use Export at the foot of this group.\n\nGive it time before you read much into it. A card you did not tap waits a day to be graded, the weights are allowed one unit of movement a day, and each source only builds numbers up while it is the one showing. A few weeks of ordinary use is the least you need before the comparison means anything.

An update is one card, graded against what you did next: at once if you played it, after a day if not. The grade nudges the weights behind that card towards it. The day\'s budget is one unit of movement, about twenty badly predicted cards, more when its guesses were close; the rest waits for a later day.\n\nOff freezes the weights and stops recording which cards you saw and tapped, so nothing new is graded. The row it built is still stored, and your plays are still logged, so History and Stats are untouched. On by default, and it runs entirely on the phone: nothing is sent anywhere.

A card counts as seen once half of it has been on screen, across the row and down the page, for half a second; a tap counts too, settled or not. Played means a listen reached the halfway grade: thirty seconds and forty five per cent of it, or a like. Tapping and leaving after ten seconds is seen, not played; a card you never tapped counts if you play that song elsewhere that day and hear it out.\n\nEvery source is logged and graded by the same rules, so the lines compare; Try both alternates two sources in one row, so both are on screen under the same conditions.

When the engine is not building what you see, it still builds its twenty cards in the background and files them away unshown. A day later they are graded against what you went on to play, and the unseen line below is what they say.\n\nOn by default. The cost is one extra build when Home loads, library read included, off the main thread. Skipped while the last unseen row is under three hours old and from the same session and day part, and skipped in battery saver. Those cards never teach the weights and never count as cards seen. Turn this off and the unseen line stops filling in.

A day after a row is built, the app lists what you chose to play between that build and the next of its kind, or a day: plays you started yourself, heard past the halfway grade, versions of one song counted once. A hit is one of those in the row\'s twenty cards.\n\nThe row had to guess a choice you made on your own, from search or your library, not only a card you tapped. Expect low numbers. The unseen line is the shadow row, scored the same way on cards nobody saw. Your library\'s row and YouTube\'s are not scored here: their cards are not stored.

Every card the engine places carries a predicted chance that you will play it, worked out from the same weights that ranked it, and lowered for cards further along the row. The Brier score is the average of the squared gap between that prediction and what happened, one for played and zero for not: zero is perfect, 0.25 is what predicting one half every time would score.\n\nMost cards are not played, so predicting a low chance for everything also scores well. The table splits cards by predicted chance into five bands so you can see which way it is wrong. Only cards the engine put on screen are counted.

Each line is one weight with its starting value in brackets. Above its start, that feature pushes a card\'s score up more; below, it pushes down more, so a penalty below its start bites harder. Five of the fourteen are penalties and can never rise above zero, and none can move more than 3 from its start.\n\nThese are the numbers added up inside the score, not percentages and not shares of anything, so read each against its own starting point rather than against the others. Five more, one per lane, are kept but not shown here. The heading counts learning steps, one per graded card applied, not songs played.

This deletes the weights table and nothing else: the numbers above go back to their starting values, the update count goes to zero, and the next row is built from those starting values. Your listen log, every card the engine recorded with its grade, the other figures under How it\'s doing, your exclusions and your settings are all kept.\n\nIt takes effect at once, with no confirmation. The day by day loop will not relearn what it lost, because it only ever applies cards it has not applied before; Rebuild is what brings the learning back.

It clears the weights, starts again from their starting values, and replays the graded cards it has applied, in the order it applied them, leaving out anything you have forgotten. That is not the same as replaying your listening: a play teaches only if it was a card the engine showed you, or a pick from the spare pool behind a row.\n\nNothing on screen says it is working; the numbers above change in place when it finishes. It is one pass over the stored cards, so a longer history takes longer. Reach for it after a Reset. Forgetting a session or a day already rebuilds for you.

A session is a run of listening with no gap longer than thirty minutes, from the end of one play to the start of the next. This takes the session of whatever is playing now, or of your most recent play, however long ago. Every play in it is marked not for learning, the grades from the cards you tapped are set to weigh nothing, and the weights are rebuilt from the start without them, so what it taught is taken back rather than merely stopped.\n\nHistory, Stats and your play counts are untouched. Cards you were shown in that session but did not play still count as passed over.

The same mechanism over a window instead of a session: every play that started between local midnight and now stops teaching, the grades from the cards you tapped are set to weigh nothing, and the weights are rebuilt from the start without them.\n\nMidnight is read from the time zone the phone is in at the moment you tap, so a clock change can move the line by an hour and travel by more. A song that started before midnight and finished after it belongs to yesterday and stays. Cards you were shown today but did not play still count as passed over.

Thirty constants, each with its default and a field: what a play must last to count, activation\'s decay, the lane shares, the seed counts, the sampling temperature. A number overrides one, an empty field restores it, Reset all clears every one. They reach the engine\'s own row only, not the learning loop. What is already on screen does not change: a build under three hours old is reused, so pull to refresh.\n\nThe collision report counts your songs, the version groups with more than one title, and the related links that pair a song with its own version. The rule ignores the artist, so two songs sharing a title merge.

The export is one JSON object: the moment you exported, how many learning steps are behind the numbers, the nineteen weights with the value each holds now, the value it started from and the bounds it may not leave, and the engine\'s shipped constants. That is all of it. No song titles, no artists, no ids, no play counts, no dates of anything you played, nothing about your account or your phone.\n\nIt is handed to Android\'s share sheet as text, so it goes to whichever app you pick there and nowhere else; nothing is uploaded. Before the engine has learned anything, the weights come out empty.

Everything below is raw material, not a verdict. It lives in the app\'s own database on this phone, in four tables: the listens, the gestures you made about songs, the cards Quick picks showed you, and the rows it built. The engine reads what it needs from them here; these tables are not uploaded anywhere. Backup and restore copies that database whole, so a backup carries this ledger and a restore brings it back. What gets written is decided under Privacy and history: Pause listen history stops every row below, and Clear listen history deletes all of it along with the weights the engine learned.

A row opens when sound starts, is written to every minute so a crash loses at most that, and closes when the song stops. Anything under two seconds of play is thrown away.\n\nCounted as a play means it passed Minimum playback duration, under Privacy and history, 30 percent of its length by default. That flag decides your history and play counts; the engine ignores it. It weighs each listen itself, ignoring anything under thirty seconds you did not like, and ramping from a tenth of the song to four fifths. The gap between them is the skipping, which the engine needs as much as the finished plays.

The boundary is thirty minutes of silence, from the end of one play to the start of the next; your converted old play log was cut the same way.\n\nA session is not a queue: it runs across several, and changing album does not start one. Sessions matter several ways: this session seeds the row; a song adds to its strength at most three times per session, so an hour on repeat does not outweigh a week; the artists of your last thirty sessions feed the feature that notices what you play together; and anything from this session that ended in the last half hour is kept out.

Ended is read off the player\'s own count of songs that reached their end, so it is exact; a repeat counts as ended. Skipped means the move to the next song was a seek, which is you. Replaced means the queue was swapped out underneath it. Stopped is everything else: paused and never resumed, the app closed, or a row left open by a crash and closed at the next launch. Unknown is a listen converted from the old play log.\n\nA play only ever adds. A skip subtracts, at half weight, and only between thirty seconds and nine tenths of the song, most sharply near the middle.

The origin belongs to the queue, not the song, so every track of an album queue reads album. Only a card tapped in Quick picks records a slot, counted from one. Autoplay depth is how many songs have run on since the last one you chose; choosing resets it to zero.\n\nIt matters because the engine multiplies a listen\'s value by how much you chose it: a search counts 1.0, anything you picked yourself 0.8, a card from a Home row 0.7, a radio track 0.6 decaying to a floor of 0.2 as the chain runs on. Songs you searched for and heard through also become seeds.

A card counts as seen when half of it is on screen, across the row and down the page, and still there half a second after you stop scrolling. Each slot counts once per build, and a tap is recorded against it.\n\nA play is only a win against what else was on screen, so the cards you passed over are what makes it one. A card seen and not played within a day is graded a loss at a third of the weight of a play. Cards you passed over in the last fortnight push that song down the row, harder each time; older sightings stop counting.

Seeking back or forward, volume up or down, repeat one on or off, adding to a playlist, downloading, sharing, opening lyrics or the artist page, and taking a song out of the queue. Each is stored with the moment; a seek or a volume change also carries how far in you were and how big it was, and a gesture made during a song is tied to that listen. Nothing leaves the phone, and Pause listen history stops all of it.\n\nThe first number is kept, not used: no part of the scoring reads these rows yet. The second, cards tapped, is the engine\'s main positive.

Each row is one listen. After the title comes how it ended, what share of its length was played, a question mark when the app never learned that length, the seconds played, and where it was started from, its slot when it had one, and, if it autoplayed, how far down the chain. If it did not pass your play threshold it says so. Last is the time it ended.\n\nThis is the audit trail: the last thirty stops, newest first, and they are the same rows the engine learns from. Older ones are still there, just not shown.

YouTube Music shows the shelf YouTube builds for your account, falling back to the library row when a load finds no shelf, offline for one. Your library ranks songs related to your last five plays, your week\'s top five and your last ten likes. Best recommendations builds the row from your listen log; with fewer than eight cards to place it says so and shows one of the other two.\n\nTry both drafts alternately, an engine card then one from the other source, never two versions of a song, and logs which side each card came from. Off removes the row. Only this row changes, nothing else on Home.

The chips sit above Quick picks when the engine\'s row is showing. Auto is the default and adds nothing: the ordinary row, fitted to the time of day. Discover fixes half the row, ten cards of twenty, to songs new to you, and ignores the Adventurousness slider. Favourites seeds only from what you have liked, so unliked songs still appear, and leans towards artists and rediscovery; the new to you lane gets none of the row.\n\nFocus, Chill and Party have nothing built in. Every play you start while one is on is stamped with it, wherever it began, and until twenty of those have been heard well the row is exactly Auto\'s. The line underneath counts tagged plays, including ones too short for that twenty. A chip stays on until you change it, and changing it rebuilds the row.

Where the Quick picks row gets its songs. YouTube Music picks them for your account. Your library builds the row instead from songs related to what you have already played. This changes that one row; the rest of the home screen is the same either way.
